items.title: Test TEST-MCP-001
items.description: Given configurable RepoRoot/Todo paths, when service starts, then path resolution is correct.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-002
items.description: Given TODO API operations, when create/update/delete/query run, then contracts remain stable.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-003
items.description: Given multi-tenant workspace configuration, when requests are made with different `X-Workspace-Path` headers, then data remains isolated per workspace on the single shared port.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-004
items.description: Given vector + FTS data, when context search executes, then hybrid results are returned.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-005
items.description: Given GitHub sync enabled, when issue sync runs, then ISSUE-* mapping is consistent.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-006
items.description: Given STDIO mode, when tool requests are sent, then parity with HTTP behavior is preserved.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-007
items.description: Given workspace registration, when a workspace is created, then its directory scaffold is created and an `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml` marker file is written to its root pointing to the shared host port.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-008
items.description: Given tool registry with tags, when keyword search runs with a singular or plural term, then matching tools from both global and workspace scopes are returned. Given default buckets in config, when the server starts for the first time, then buckets are seeded and idempotent on subsequent starts.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-009
items.description: Given per-workspace auth tokens and `X-Workspace-Path` header resolution, when a request to any `/mcpserver/*` endpoint lacks `X-Api-Key`, then the server returns 401. When a valid token is provided, workspace resolution uses the three-tier chain: `X-Workspace-Path` header → API key reverse lookup → default workspace.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-010
items.description: Given valid pairing credentials, when the `/pair` login flow completes, then an HttpOnly session cookie is issued and the API key is returned. Given constant-time comparison, when two passwords of the same length differ by one character, then timing side-channel is not exploitable.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-011
items.description: Given a configured tunnel provider, when the hosted service starts, then the tunnel process launches and `GetStatusAsync` returns a public URL. When the service stops, the process is terminated within 5 s.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-012
items.description: Given an MCP client connecting to `/mcp-transport`, when a tool call is made, then the response is semantically equivalent to the corresponding REST endpoint result. Given a request without the required `Accept` header, then the endpoint returns 406.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-013
items.description: Given a workspace, when `StartAsync` completes, then `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml` exists at the workspace root with the shared host port, endpoint paths, and auth token. When `StopAsync` completes, then the marker file is removed.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-014
items.description: Given a TODO item with a title and description, when `RequirementsService.AnalyzeAsync` is called, then `ExtractRequirementIds` correctly parses both JSON-block and regex-fallback response formats and returns distinct, non-empty FR/TR ID lists.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-015
items.description: Given a Markdown file with a `# Session Log - {title}` header, when `MarkdownSessionLogParser.TryParse` is called, then it returns a `UnifiedSessionLogDto` with matching title, model, status, and at least one entry. Given a file without the header, then `TryParse` returns null.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-026
items.description: Given a CQRS Dispatcher with a registered command handler, when `SendAsync` is called with a valid command, then the handler is invoked and `Result<T>.IsSuccess` is true with the expected value.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-027
items.description: Given a CQRS command handler that returns `Result.Failure(error)`, when the Dispatcher processes the result, then it logs at Warning level with the error message and correlation context.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-028
items.description: Given a CQRS command handler that throws an exception, when the Dispatcher catches it, then `Result<T>.IsFailure` is true, `Result<T>.Exception` is set, and the Dispatcher logs at Error level with exception details.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-029
items.description: Given a new `CorrelationId`, when `Next()` is called multiple times, then the base ID remains stable and the counter increments sequentially. Given a correlation string `"12345678.3"`, when `CorrelationId.Parse` is called, then `BaseId` is `12345678` and the counter is `3`.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-030
items.description: Given a `CallContext` used as `ILogger`, when `LogInformation` is called, then the log entry is captured in `CallContext.LogEntries` with the correct level, message, and timestamp. Given the Dispatcher's `ILoggerProvider`, when a `DispatcherLogger` emits a log with a correlation scope, then the structured output includes `correlationBaseId` and `correlationStep` as separate fields.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-031
items.description: Given two pipeline behaviors registered in order, when a command is dispatched, then the first behavior's pre-processing runs before the second, and the second's post-processing runs before the first's. Given a behavior that returns `Result.Failure` without calling `next`, then the handler is never invoked.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-032
items.description: Given an empty database, when `AgentService.SeedBuiltInDefaultsAsync` is called, then 7 built-in agent definitions are created. Given a database already containing built-in agents, when `SeedBuiltInDefaultsAsync` is called again, then no duplicates are created (idempotent).

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-033
items.description: Given the AgentService, when `UpsertDefinitionAsync` creates a new definition and `GetDefinitionAsync` retrieves it, then all fields match. When `DeleteDefinitionAsync` is called on a non-built-in definition, then it succeeds. When called on a built-in definition, then it returns `IsFailure` with an appropriate error.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-034
items.description: Given a workspace with an agent configured, when `BanAgentAsync` is called with `Global = false`, then only that workspace's agent is banned. When called with `Global = true`, then all workspaces with that agent are banned. When `UnbanAgentAsync` is called, then the agent is re-enabled.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-035
items.description: Given a Director `LoginHandler`, when the device authorization flow completes successfully, then `Result<LoginResult>.IsSuccess` is true and the token is cached. When the flow times out, then `Result<LoginResult>.IsFailure` with an appropriate error.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-036
items.description: Given a Director `LaunchAgentHandler`, when the agent is enabled and not banned, then the agent process is spawned and `Result<LaunchResult>.IsSuccess`. When the agent is banned, then `Result<LaunchResult>.IsFailure` with a ban reason.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-037
items.description: Given a Director `InitWorkspaceHandler`, when called on a valid workspace path, then `agents.yaml` is created and agents are registered via the MCP Server API. When the workspace path doesn't exist, then `Result.IsFailure`.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-038
items.description: Given a Director `BanAgentHandler`, when called with a valid agent ID and reason, then the MCP Server API is called to ban the agent and a Ban event is logged. When the agent doesn't exist, then `Result.IsFailure`.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-039
items.description: Given seeded canonical requirements docs, when `RequirementsDocumentService` loads them, then FR/TR/TEST/mapping entries are parsed correctly and generated Markdown preserves the canonical header and entry formats.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-040
items.description: Given `/mcpserver/requirements` CRUD endpoints, when an FR entry is created, generated via `/mcpserver/requirements/generate?doc=functional`, and deleted, then the generated document reflects each mutation and the deleted entry is no longer returned.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-041
items.description: Given /mcpserver/requirements/generate?doc=all, when the endpoint is called, then it writes Functional-Requirements.md, Technical-Requirements.md, Testing-Requirements.md, TR-per-FR-Mapping.md, and Requirements-Matrix.md to the workspace, preserves existing matrix rows, appends missing FR/TR/TEST IDs, and returns export metadata.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-042
items.description: Given concurrent requirement mutations, when `RequirementsDocumentService` persists updates, then writes remain atomic and the resulting Markdown files remain parseable without temp-file residue.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-043
items.description: Given MCP STDIO requirements tools (`requirements_list`, `requirements_generate`, `requirements_create`, `requirements_update`, `requirements_delete`), when agents invoke them, then results are semantically equivalent to the corresponding REST requirements endpoints.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-044
items.description: Given the three-tier workspace resolution chain, when `X-Workspace-Path` header is present, then it takes priority over API key reverse lookup; when absent, API key resolves workspace; when neither is present, the default workspace is used.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-045
items.description: Given EF Core global query filter on `WorkspaceId`, when entities are inserted for workspace A and queried from workspace B context, then workspace A's entities are not visible from workspace B.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-046
items.description: Given the Director client with `WorkspacePath` set, when API calls are made, then the `X-Workspace-Path` header is sent on all requests and workspace switching only changes the header, not the base URL.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-047
items.description: Given the typed client library with `McpServerClientOptions.WorkspacePath` set, when requests are sent, then the `X-Workspace-Path` header is present alongside `X-Api-Key`.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-048
items.description: Given a TODO item in workspace A, when `POST /mcpserver/todo/{id}/move` is called with `targetWorkspacePath` pointing to workspace B, then the item is created in workspace B with all fields preserved and deleted from workspace A. Given an invalid target workspace path, then the endpoint returns 400.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-049
items.description: Given voice conversation endpoints, when a session is created with a `DeviceId`, then `GET /mcpserver/voice/session?deviceId=` returns the active session. When `DELETE` is called, then the session is destroyed and subsequent status queries return 404.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-050
items.description: Given an active voice session, when `POST /mcpserver/voice/session/{id}/turn` is called with transcript text, then a `VoiceTurnResponse` is returned with assistant text. When `POST /mcpserver/voice/session/{id}/turn/stream` is called, then SSE events are streamed with `type` values of `chunk`, `tool_status`, `done`, or `error`.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-051
items.description: Given a voice session with `SessionIdleTimeoutMinutes` configured, when the session is idle beyond the timeout, then the `IdleShutdownCommand` is sent and the session is terminated. Given a device with an active session, when a new session is requested for the same device, then the existing session is returned (one-per-device enforcement).

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-052
items.description: Given a Windows service running as LocalSystem, when `DesktopProcessLauncher.LaunchWithStdio` is called, then a process is created on the interactive desktop with redirected stdio pipes via `CreateProcessAsUser`. Given `LaunchVisible`, then a visible console window is created.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-053
items.description: Given an `appsettings.yaml` file with configuration overrides, when the server starts, then YAML values override `appsettings.json` values for matching keys. Given the YAML file is absent, then startup succeeds using JSON configuration only.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-054
items.description: Given the template service with a YAML file, when `GET /mcpserver/templates` is called with optional `category`, `tag`, and `keyword` query parameters, then a filtered list of `PromptTemplate` items is returned. When no filters are provided, all templates are returned.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-055
items.description: Given a valid `PromptTemplateCreateRequest`, when `POST /mcpserver/templates` is called, then a new template is persisted to YAML and returned with 201 Created. When a duplicate ID is submitted, then 409 Conflict is returned. When `PUT /mcpserver/templates/{id}` is called with partial update fields, only specified fields are changed. When `DELETE /mcpserver/templates/{id}` is called, the template is removed.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-056
items.description: Given a stored template with Handlebars content and declared variables, when `POST /mcpserver/templates/{id}/test` is called with variable values, then `PromptTemplateTestResult` contains the rendered content. When required variables are missing, then `MissingVariables` is populated and `Success` is false. When `POST /mcpserver/templates/test` is called with inline template content, the inline content is rendered without requiring a stored template.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-057
items.description: Given the Director TUI with a Templates tab, when `TemplateListViewModel.RefreshCommand` executes, then the CQRS `ListTemplatesQuery` flows through `ListTemplatesQueryHandler` → `ITemplateApiClient` → `TemplateClient` → REST API and populates the table view. When a template is selected and the test action is invoked via `TemplateDetailViewModel`, then `TestTemplateQuery` renders the template and displays output.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-058
items.description: Given `FileMarkerPromptProvider` with a valid `templates/default-marker-prompt.hbs.yaml` file, when `GetGlobalPromptTemplateAsync` is called, then the template content is returned and cached. When the file is missing, then `null` is returned and `MarkerFileService.DefaultPromptTemplate` is used as fallback.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-059
items.description: Given `TodoPromptProvider` with todo prompt templates stored in `IPromptTemplateService` by well-known IDs (`todo-status-prompt`, `todo-implement-prompt`, `todo-plan-prompt`), when the provider is queried, then file-loaded content is returned. When templates are missing from the store, then `TodoPromptDefaults` built-in constants are returned as fallback.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-060
items.description: Given `PairingHtmlRenderer` with pairing HTML templates stored in `IPromptTemplateService` by well-known IDs (`pairing-login-page`, `pairing-key-page`, `pairing-not-configured-page`), when rendering methods are called with substitution parameters, then `{errorBanner}`, `{apiKey}`, and `{serverUrl}` tokens are replaced. When templates are missing, then `PairingHtml` static method output is returned as fallback.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-061
items.description: Given `Mcp:AgentPool:Agents` configuration, when options bind and validate, then each definition accepts `AgentName`, `AgentPath`, `AgentModel`, `AgentSeed`, `AgentParameters`, `IsInteractiveDefault`, `IsTodoPlanDefault`, `IsTodoStatusDefault`, and `IsTodoImplementDefault`. Duplicate `AgentName` values (case-insensitive) or ambiguous defaults fail validation.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-062
items.description: Given one-shot or interactive requests with no `AgentName`, when context is `Plan`, `Status`, `Implement`, or `AdHoc`, then the default agent mapped for that intent is selected. Given an explicit `AgentName`, explicit assignment overrides default routing.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-063
items.description: Given one-shot request payloads, when both `promptTemplateId` and ad-hoc `promptText` are supplied or both are missing without resolvable context template, then the API returns 400. Given template-resolved mode, missing `id` returns 400.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-064
items.description: Given one-shot context without template ID, when context is `Plan`, `Status`, or `Implement`, then existing context-based template resolution is used. Given context `AdHoc` without template ID and no ad-hoc prompt text, then the API returns 400.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-065
items.description: Given prompt resolution requests with template ID, caller values, workspace-context values, and `id`, when rendering executes, then output includes `{id}` substitution and caller values override workspace-context values on key conflicts.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-066
items.description: Given no eligible pooled agent is idle, when one-shot requests are enqueued, then requests remain `queued` and transition to `processing` once an eligible agent becomes available, followed by terminal states (`completed`, `failed`, or `canceled`).

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-067
items.description: Given queue operations, when move up/down is requested for queued items, then order changes correctly; when requested for the currently processing item, the operation is rejected. Cancel/remove semantics correctly update queue state and persisted metadata.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-068
items.description: Given pool lifecycle transitions, when queued/processing/completed/failed events occur, then notification SSE emits events in order with payload fields `AgentName`, `LastRequestPrompt`, and `SessionId`.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-069
items.description: Given multiple clients connected to a read-only response stream, when one client disconnects, then remaining subscribers continue receiving stream data and active pooled work is unaffected.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-070
items.description: Given a pooled agent processing a one-shot request, when an interactive voice connection targets that agent, then interactive linkage is established without canceling or reassigning the one-shot operation.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-071
items.description: Given an interactive stream connection, when the client disconnects, then `User is AFK.` is sent to the agent. When the client reconnects and stream establishment completes, then `User is here.` is sent. These messages are not sent for one-shot sessions.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-072
items.description: Given Director Agent Pool tab actions (connect, recycle, stop/start, queue move up/down, cancel/remove, free-form enqueue), when invoked from UI commands, then the correct REST endpoints are called and UI state refreshes from server snapshots and notifications.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-073
items.description: Given `McpServer.Support.Mcp` stateful services and registries, when architecture validation runs, then each authoritative data source is DI-owned (`singleton`/`scoped`), no stateful service is created outside DI, change notifications use `INotifyPropertyChanged`, and consumers pull current state from the source-of-truth service.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-074
items.description: Given TODO create/update and session log submit/append requests, when IDs violate canonical naming formats (`TODO persisted ids: ^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]*(?:-[A-Z0-9]+)+-\d{3}$ or ^ISSUE-\d+$`, `sessionId: <Agent>-<yyyyMMddTHHmmssZ>-<suffix>`, `requestId: req-<yyyyMMddTHHmmssZ>-<slugOrOrdinal>`), then APIs reject with validation errors and no data mutation occurs; valid IDs are accepted across YAML and SQLite TODO backends.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-075
items.description: Given `ChannelChangeEventBus`, when events are published with zero, one, or multiple subscribers, then publish does not throw and each active subscriber receives events independently; canceled subscriptions stop enumeration.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-076
items.description: Given TODO, session log, and repo mutation services, when create/update/delete-style operations succeed, then each service publishes one change event with the expected category/action/entityId values.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-077
items.description: Given extended mutation services (`ToolRegistryService`, `WorkspaceService`, `AgentService`), when representative create/update operations succeed, then each service publishes the expected category/action event.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-078
items.description: Given `GET /mcpserver/events`, when a client subscribes, then the response content type is `text/event-stream`.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-079
items.description: Given `GET /mcpserver/events?category=todo`, when a TODO change event is published, then the stream includes an `event: todo` payload containing the matching entity ID.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-080
items.description: Given category filtering on `/mcpserver/events`, when non-matching categories are published, then filtered subscribers do not receive those non-matching domain events.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-081
items.description: Given workspace-scoped GitHub auth endpoints, when a token is set via `PUT /mcpserver/gh/auth/token`, then `GET /mcpserver/gh/auth/status` reports `hasStoredToken=true`; when `DELETE /mcpserver/gh/auth/token` is called, the token is removed.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-082
items.description: Given GitHub OAuth bootstrap endpoints, when `GET /mcpserver/gh/oauth/config` is called, then effective configuration fields are returned; when OAuth is not fully configured, `GET /mcpserver/gh/oauth/authorize-url` returns 400 with a clear error.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-083
items.description: Given `GitHubCliService` with a stored workspace token, when GitHub commands are executed, then `IProcessRunner` receives a `ProcessRunRequest` containing `GitHubTokenOverride`; when no token exists and fallback is enabled, standard CLI execution is used.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-084
items.description: Given GitHub Actions workflow operations, when list/detail/rerun/cancel paths are invoked, then gh CLI commands and REST/client contracts for `/mcpserver/gh/actions/runs*` remain consistent and parse expected run/job/step metadata.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-085
items.description: Given natural-language workspace policy directives, when `POST /mcpserver/workspace/policy` or `workspace_policy_apply` is invoked with valid directives, then targeted workspace ban lists are mutated and invalid directives return structured 400 errors.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-086
items.description: Given audited copilot decoration, when invoke and streaming operations execute, then session-log submissions include `copilot_invocation` actions and completed status records.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-087
items.description: Given ingestion options and marker prompt generation for this repository, when host configuration post-processing runs, then repo-local src/McpServer.Cqrs and src/McpServer.Cqrs.Mvvm glob patterns are enforced, and marker output includes the Available Capabilities section without McpServer.UI.Core or McpServer.Director entries.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-088
items.description: Given direct website URL ingestion requests, when `POST /mcpserver/context/ingest-website` or `context_ingest_website` runs, then valid HTTP/HTTPS pages ingest as `external-web` sources, URL outcomes are returned, SSRF/private/link-local targets are blocked, redirects are bounded, and source dedup/update behavior is preserved by source key.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-089
items.description: Given a .NET 9 host application that registers the hosted Microsoft Agent Framework library against an MCP Server workspace, when the built-in agent workflow runs, then session log turns are created/updated through canonical identifiers, TODO plan/status/implementation operations execute through the existing MCP Server contracts, repository read/list/write tools browse repo-relative paths without host-specific glue code, local desktop process launch reuses the authenticated workspace desktop-launch contract, `mcp_powershell_session_*` tools execute commands inside a persistent in-process PowerShell session hosted by the agent itself, and host applications can drive the same local runspace interactively through `IMcpHostedAgent.PowerShellSessions`.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-090
items.description: Given representative controller and middleware failure paths across the server, when an unhandled exception produces HTTP 500, then the response body contains a non-empty detailed error description for the failed operation, excludes secrets and raw stack traces, and remains consistent across endpoints through the shared error-handling path.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-091
items.description: Given the admin configuration management surface, when configuration values are read or patched through the configuration controller and YAML helper, then effective settings are exposed as flattened key-value pairs, submitted YAML-backed keys are persisted and reloaded, and standard JWT Bearer admin authorization keeps the endpoints unavailable when OIDC is disabled.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-092
items.description: Given a TODO create request with id `ISSUE-NEW`, when GitHub issue creation succeeds, then the server persists the TODO using the canonical `ISSUE-{number}` id returned by GitHub, includes GitHub correlation metadata in the TODO note, and returns the canonical id from the create surface instead of the temporary alias.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-093
items.description: Given workspace-scoped GitHub CLI execution, when gh commands run with either a stored workspace token or fallback authentication, then the process runner receives the resolved workspace root as the working directory.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-094
items.description: Given an existing `ISSUE-{number}` TODO updated through any server TODO update surface, when the local update succeeds, then the server preserves the existing description, syncs title/state/priority metadata back to GitHub using canonical `priority: HIGH|MEDIUM|LOW` labels, and posts a GitHub issue comment describing the applied change set.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-095
items.description: Given an `ISSUE-NEW` TODO created through the HTTP API, when GitHub-origin comments are added and GitHub-to-TODO sync runs, then the TODO note gains the generated GitHub comment section without altering the TODO description. When the TODO priority changes and a TODO-authored note comment is appended, then the GitHub issue receives the canonical updated priority label and a GitHub comment containing the appended note text. When the GitHub issue is later closed externally and GitHub-to-TODO sync runs again, then the TODO is marked done.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-096
items.description: Given an empty authoritative SQLite TODO store and an existing `TODO.yaml`, when initialization runs and later authoritative mutations project back to YAML, then bootstrap import, deterministic projection ordering, projection-only YAML behavior, and preservation of `notes`, `completed`, and `code-review-remediation` metadata are all verified by automated tests.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-097
items.description: Given a TODO item mutated through create/update/delete and queried through storage, REST, typed client, and integration surfaces, when audit history is requested, then append-only ordered states, delete-history retention, not-found behavior, and explicit projection-failure classification are all verified by automated tests.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-098
items.description: Given a Parseable-bound log event with more than 250 structured properties and user properties that collide with reserved Parseable field names, when `ParseableEventFormatter` serializes the event, then the payload contains at most 250 top-level fields, canonical reserved metadata is preserved, and overflow non-reserved properties are deterministically omitted.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-100
items.description: Given a PowerShell `McpSession` workspace with an active session cached in `.mcpSession/current-session.json`, when the legacy `.mcpServer/session.yaml` wrapper is missing and the module is reinitialized or resolves a session without an explicit `Session` argument, then it reuses the cached current session object and session ID. When the session is completed, both cache files are removed.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-101
items.description: Given trust-bootstrap marker rendering and the public PowerShell bootstrap modules, when the marker signature is valid and `/health` echoes the submitted nonce exactly, then `McpSession`, `McpTodo`, and `McpContext` initialize successfully and proceed with MCP usage. When the signature is invalid or the nonce does not match, then each bootstrap module emits `MCP_UNTRUSTED`, does not probe additional endpoints, and aborts MCP usage before session-log or TODO traffic continues.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-102
items.description: Given the provider-factory, native encryption, and maintenance-command workstreams, when SQLite, PostgreSQL, and SQL Server are configured for clean-database integration runs, then provider-specific migrations apply successfully and the live encryption state matches the configured state. When encryption is enabled or disabled on an existing database, then the provider-specific transition workflow shall expose a no-data-loss maintenance procedure and dry-run plan before mutation, with automated dry-run tests covering SQLite SEE, PostgreSQL `pg_tde`, and SQL Server TDE command generation. SQL Server provider and migration integration coverage shall use a self-managed SQL Server LocalDB instance created and torn down by the test harness where LocalDB is installed, and otherwise a temporary SQL Server 2025 Developer instance the harness starts for the run and removes afterwards (operator decision 2026-10-15: "allow a temporary sql server 2025 dev instance when necessary."), while SQL Server TDE validation shall run against a separate non-LocalDB SQL Server target because LocalDB cannot validate TDE.

acceptanceCriteria.text: SqlServerSandboxPlanAssertion_AcceptsLocalDbOrTemporaryInstanceAndRejectsSharedOrNone, then the harness itself: the SQL Server cases use a self-managed LocalDB instance when SqlLocalDB is installed and otherwise a temporary SQL Server 2025 Developer instance the harness starts for the run and removes afterwards, each case on its own uniquely named database that is dropped; a shared server, no server, and a skip are rejected (PLAN-SESSIONTRIAGEFIX-001 B11, triage-report-ead2fdaa).

SqlServer_CleanDatabase_AppliesMigrationsAndPersistsEntity (renamed from SqlServer_LocalDb_CleanDatabase_AppliesMigrationsAndPersistsEntity), HandoffIngestionStorageMigrationTests.SqlServer_HandoffMigration_DowngradeAndReupgrade and HostileReviewG4OverlayTests.HostileReviewEntity_RoundTrip_SqlitePgSqlServer pass on LAB-OMARCHY through the temporary instance and on PAYTON-LEGION2 through LocalDB (PLAN-SESSIONTRIAGEFIX-001 B11).

RecoveryRunDeletedAtAssertion_AcceptsDatetime2UtcRoundTripAndRejectsOffsetColumnOrShiftedInstant, then SqlServer_RequirementsRecoveryRun_SoftDelete_RoundTripsUtcDeletedAt: on a clean SQL Server database migrated to head, RequirementsRecoveryRuns.DeletedAtUtc is datetime2 (the AddHostileReviewTables AlterColumn) and a soft-deleted recovery run reads back its DeletedAtUtc as the same UTC instant (TR-MCP-DB-DTO-001; PLAN-SESSIONTRIAGEFIX-001 B8, triage-report-71d801ad). The gate accepts a datetime2 column whose read-back equals the written instant at offset zero, and rejects a datetimeoffset column, a shifted instant, a non-zero offset and a missing value.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-103
items.description: Given a Byrd execution TODO, when unit tests are not defined, then the service rejects transition to `Implementing`; when unit tests are defined through the test-plan API, then the TODO advances to `TestReady`.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-104
items.description: Given a Byrd execution TODO linked to requirements, session turns, and modified files, when bounded execution context or checkpoint delta context is requested, then the server returns only concise snippets, recent turn summaries, relevant files, artifacts, commits, and updated next action for that TODO.

items.title: Test TEST-MCP-PLUGININT-001
items.description: A shared deterministic Theory and companion AiTheory matrix must exercise the real Session Log workflow for all supported agent plugins.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The deterministic matrix gives each PowerShell host (Codex, ClaudeCode, ClaudeCowork, Copilot, Grok) its scenario session id <AgentSourceType>-<yyyyMMddTHHmmssZ>-pluginint through MCP_SESSION_ID, the plugins' own session-id input (New-ReplPluginSessionId and New-PluginSessionId read it first), from its first plugin call, so bootstrap, openSession and every later verb persist under that id and Theory_Agent_BootstrapBeginAppendComplete_CapturesIdsCacheShaReceipt captures it; Node hosts are unchanged (triage-report-914a2812; PLAN-SESSIONTRIAGEFIX-001 E5; tests in tests/QBrainAi.PluginIntegration.Tests/PluginScenarioSessionIdTests.cs: ScenarioSessionEnvironmentAssertion_AcceptsPinnedIdAndRejectsMissingOtherOrSuffixOnly, ScenarioSessionEnvironment_PowerShellHosts_CarryScenarioSessionId, ScenarioSessionEnvironment_NodeHosts_Unchanged; and the five PowerShell rows of Theory_Agent_BootstrapBeginAppendComplete_CapturesIdsCacheShaReceipt).

Each docs/receipts/pluginint-p20-* receipt carries, committed beside its summary.json, the harness log that summary names (logFile), byte-identical to the log the P20 harness wrote; the repository's ignore rules do not exclude docs/receipts/pluginint-p20-*/harness.log although *.log stays ignored elsewhere, and PluginUpdateServiceHarnessTests reads the newest receipt's log (UpdateService, sanitized, Failed 0, Skipped 0) (triage-report-96ea2f71; PLAN-SESSIONTRIAGEFIX-001 E2; tests: PluginSessionLogHarness_AgainstUpdateService_SanitizedFixtures_FailedZeroSkippedZero, and git check-ignore on both receipt logs as recorded evidence).

The harness writes to every plugin host process's stdin as UTF-8 without a byte order mark (NodeMcpStdioSession for the Node MCP stdio host, RealPluginProcessRunner for the others), so the first JSON-RPC line a Node MCP stdio host reads (initialize) is plain JSON its SDK parses, and the Cline v1 session initializes instead of timing out (triage-report-fbac91dc; PLAN-SESSIONTRIAGEFIX-001 E4; root cause measured 2026-10-15: with StandardInputEncoding Encoding.UTF8 .NET 10 writes EF BB BF before the first line on a pipe; tests in tests/QBrainAi.PluginIntegration.Tests/PluginStdinEncodingTests.cs: StdinEncodingAssertion_AcceptsBomFreeAndRejectsBomPrefixed, PluginHostStdin_Encoding_HasNoPreamble, RealPluginProcessRunner_ChildStdin_StartsWithJson; and the Cline rows of the deterministic matrix).

The AI lane's aiUnit strategy names a command the operating system running the lane can start (Linux: an executable PowerShell script with a pwsh shebang; Windows: a .cmd launcher), present in the test output folder, and that command asks grok for the plugin evaluator's own JSON: a schema requiring valid (boolean), missingFields and contradictions (string arrays) and allowing nothing else, with the prompt aiUnit passes kept intact as one argument and grok's structured output returned, so every host's AI-lane receipt carries the model's verdict and a receipt the model judges invalid fails the lane; QBrainAi.Review.Tests keeps its own wrapper (triage-report-3546932eb5e94bbc8602fcb586cf5d5b, BUG-BASELINE-017; PLAN-SESSIONTRIAGEFIX-001 E6; operator decision 2026-10-15 "Launch + evaluator schema"; tests in tests/QBrainAi.PluginIntegration.Tests/AiEvaluatorStrategyTests.cs: EvaluatorStrategyAssertion_AcceptsStartableEvaluatorAndRejectsCmdOnUnixMissingOrReviewSchema, EvaluatorStrategy_OutputFolder_NamesStartableCommand, EvaluatorWrapper_FakeGrok_SendsEvaluatorSchemaAndReturnsStructuredOutput; and the eight AiTheory_Agent_RequiresValidJsonFields rows of the AI lane). The evaluator's instructions state the receipt contract: agent, cacheFolder, entrypoint and status (completed) are required non-empty strings, sessionId, requestId and sourceSha identify the persisted turn, and deterministicFailure is optional and false when absent, so missingFields names only required fields that are absent or empty; the evaluation waits for the active strategy's TimeoutSeconds (one setting, 120 seconds against measured grok latencies of 28.7 to 59.3 seconds) plus a 30-second margin, inside the theory's 240-second timeout; the strategy names no model or temperature, so grok runs its default model (operator rule 2026-10-15: requirements name no model) (PLAN-SESSIONTRIAGEFIX-001 E6 follow-up after pluginint-20261015T1311, where 5 of 8 AI rows failed, 2 on the 60-second wait and 3 on missingFields=deterministicFailure; tests: EvaluatorContractAssertion_AcceptsStatedContractAndRejectsUnstatedOrRequiredFlag, EvaluatorWaitAssertion_AcceptsStrategyTimeoutPlusMarginAndRejectsFixedOrOverBudget, EvaluatorStrategyModelAssertion_AcceptsNoModelSpecAndRejectsPinnedModelOrTemperature, EvaluatorPrompt_Fixture_StatesReceiptContract, EvaluatorWait_Fixture_UsesStrategyTimeoutWithinTheoryBudget).

Each docs/receipts/pluginint-p19-* receipt carries, committed beside its summary.json, every log its P19 run wrote there: the native-suite logs its plugins and afterSync rows name (logFile) and, where the run kept one, its sync-agent-plugins.log (which the C-green-P19 review read), each byte-identical to the log the run wrote; the repository's ignore rules do not exclude docs/receipts/pluginint-p19-*/*.log although *.log stays ignored elsewhere, and PluginNativeSuiteReceiptTests reads the newest receipt's logs (the eight official plugins before and after SyncAgentPlugins, each Failed 0 and Skipped 0) (PLAN-SESSIONTRIAGEFIX-001 E7, the E2 sibling the integration lane run pluginint-20261015T1151 found; operator 2026-10-15 "Fix issues correctly"; tests: PluginNativeSuite_EachOfficialPlugin_FailedZeroSkippedZero and PluginNativeSuite_AfterSyncAgentPlugins_FailedZeroSkippedZero, and as recorded evidence git check-ignore and each copy's SHA-256 against its PAYTON-LEGION2 original).

The harness starts PowerShell plugin hosts through the PowerShell executable name each operating system provides, pwsh.exe on Windows and pwsh elsewhere, so the matrix needs no pwsh.exe alias on Linux (PLAN-SESSIONTRIAGEFIX-001 E8, operator decision 2026-10-15 "Fix them in this plan"; observed: PluginHostProcessAdapter.cs line 82 named pwsh.exe on every operating system, and LAB-OMARCHY passed only through its ~/.local/bin/pwsh.exe and /usr/local/bin/pwsh.exe symlinks; tests: PowerShellHostExecutableAssertion_AcceptsPerOsNameAndRejectsFixedName, PluginHostProcessAdapter_PowerShellHost_UsesOsExecutableName, and the PowerShell rows of Adapter_CapturesExecutableArgsStdinEnvCwdTimeoutExitStdoutStderr).

items.description: Provider-backed and production-entrypoint tests must prove deterministic dry-run, atomic mixed apply, rollback, stale-precondition rejection, idempotent replay, concurrency safety, exact audit readback, and synchronized supported-plugin behavior.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A mixed create, update, delete, acceptance-criteria, mapping-upsert, and mapping-delete plan commits once and exact post-query state and counts match the approved dry-run.
Injected validation and persistence failures at each operation class leave the effective requirements, criteria, mappings, idempotency state, and audit state byte-equivalent to the pre-state.
Stale pre-state hash, duplicate operations, missing references, and idempotency-key content mismatch are rejected before mutation with stable classified errors.
Dry-run is mutation-free, identical replay returns the original receipt, and repeated post-state queries contain no duplicates or drift.
Two concurrent plans using the same pre-state prove that at most one commits and the loser receives a stale-precondition outcome without partial state.
All supported production plugin entrypoints that advertise requirements operations execute the canonical dry-run and apply fixtures with identical normalized results, zero failures, and zero skips.

A zero-skip matrix executes mixed commit, validation rollback, persistence rollback, stale precondition, idempotent replay, and concurrent-plan cases against SQLite, SQL Server, and PostgreSQL. Every provider row proves exact raw and effective post-state plus audit and idempotency state.

Layered fixtures containing inherited, shadowed, and out-of-bounds records prove that dry-run binds every scope and layer field, apply writes only the target layer, and any change to bound raw state, effective state, layer metadata, or scope bounds produces a no-mutation stale-precondition result.
